strengths: Addresses an important and under-explored gap: systematically isolating and evaluating mathematical perception separate from reasoning in MLLMs
Well-designed benchmark with comprehensive coverage: 4 complementary perception tasks across 3 domains, multiple question formats, quality-verified annotations
Thorough and rigorous empirical evaluation: 15 models assessed, detailed ablation studies (5 key factors), systematic error categorization (CoT vs. recognition), concrete failure case analysis
GeoPeP dataset contribution: 200K structured image-text pairs addressing concrete limitations of prior caption-based approaches (MAVIS, AutoGeo) with explicit geometric annotations
Demonstrates clear perception-reasoning connection with consistent ~4% gains on MathVista/MathVerse and analysis showing how perception bottlenecks propagate to reasoning errors
Substantial practical improvements on fine-grained grounding (+79% for SVE-Math-DeepSeek+) showing targeted training can address specific perceptual gaps
Comprehensive presentation with detailed appendices (problem templates, case studies, visualizations) supporting reproducibility and community adoption
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: benchmark reuses existing datasets (CLEVR, FigureQA) with reformatting; synthetic geometry generation is straightforward; structured annotations in GeoPeP are intuitive extensions rather than novel methods

Modest downstream improvements undercut impact claims: ~4% reasoning gains are non-trivial but limited relative to the perception improvements, raising questions about perception-reasoning transfer; MAVIS variant hurts performance (Table 6) without sufficient investigation

Narrow scope: heavy focus on synthetic 2D geometric diagrams; missing important mathematical domains (calculus, probability, complex statistics); no coverage of real-world diagram diversity (handwritten, varied styles); only fixed IoU grounding without partial credit analysis

Incomplete experimental design and unfair comparisons: only SVE-Math-DeepSeek fine-tuned with GeoPeP (other math MLLMs untested); inconsistent inference settings; no statistical significance testing or error bars; missing ablation separating structured annotation effect from dataset size

Insufficient analysis of generalization: no investigation of what GeoPeP components (shapes, relationships, coordinates) matter most; unclear how synthetic geometry improvements transfer to real diagrams; ablation studies limited to plane geometry only

Generalization gaps not addressed: why MAVIS hurts reasoning unexplained; which perception improvements actually contribute to reasoning unclear; comparison with specialized perception/grounding models absent; no inter-annotator agreement reported

Reproducibility concerns: 200K dataset composition across domains not specified; construction details for solid geometry/graphs underspecified; potential data leakage from CLEVR/FigureQA pre-training not fully addressed; project URL incomplete in manuscript

strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly identifies the gap that existing benchmarks conflate perception with reasoning, making it unclear whether performance reflects genuine diagram understanding

Comprehensive benchmark design: multiple perception tasks (classification, counting, grounding, relationships) across diverse domains (plane geometry, solid geometry, graphs) with structured annotations and human verification
Extensive empirical evaluation: 15 diverse MLLMs tested with detailed ablation studies on key perceptual factors (object count, visual quality, distractors, CoT reasoning)
Concrete error analysis: systematic categorization of model failures with specific examples differentiating Chain-of-Thought errors from recognition errors
GeoPeP shows practical value: structured annotation approach yields measurable improvements in both perception (23-35% gains over baselines) and downstream mathematical reasoning (~4% on MathVista)
Strong presentation: effective visualizations of perception gaps and clear exposition of experimental methodology
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core idea of isolating perception is straightforward; four tasks are standard computer vision operations; benchmark design uses conventional template-based generation without methodological innovation
Synthetic data dominance and scale: 66% of benchmark is purely synthetic plane geometry with only ~800 unique images; raises questions about real-world diagram complexity and diversity
GeoPeP's incremental contribution: structured annotations (shapes, locations, relationships) represent an obvious approach rather than methodological advance; two-stage training is standard practice
Data composition unclear: GeoPeP's construction largely unexplained—appears to be mostly/all synthetic; paper lacks details on data sourcing, composition, and diversity

Modest empirical improvements: 68.4% on plane geometry still represents substantial error; ~4% improvement on MathVista is useful but not compelling; grounding remains difficult (88.4%) even with training

Findings are predictable: that synthetic diagrams challenge natural-image models, that structured data helps, and that CoT can hurt perception tasks are largely expected without deep mechanistic insight into why

Incomplete causal analysis: paper identifies that text distractors cause >20% drops while visual ones cause 2-6%, but provides no investigation into why; limited exploration of what makes diagram perception fundamentally challenging
Single base model focus: most training experiments use only SVE-Math-DeepSeek; unclear whether findings generalize to other architectures and model families
Lack of statistical rigor: no significance testing, error bars, or multiple runs reported; unfair inference settings across models acknowledged but not resolved
No novel solutions: paper identifies problems but proposes only straightforward application of existing techniques (structured data); no new architectures, losses, or methodological innovations

strengths: Clearly identifies and addresses an important gap: existing benchmarks conflate perception with reasoning, making this benchmark a valuable methodological contribution
Comprehensive, high-quality benchmark with 1,198 images and 1,609 questions across multiple perception tasks and domains with rigorous human verification
Extensive evaluation of 15 state-of-the-art MLLMs with systematic analysis of 5 key perceptual factors, revealing critical failures and actionable insights
Innovative synthetic data generation pipeline with mathematical consistency verification enabling controlled generation of diverse geometric scenarios
Well-designed GeoPeP training dataset with explicit structured annotations (shapes, relationships, coordinates) showing significant improvements: +79% on grounding, +4% on MathVista
Insightful error analysis categorizing CoT vs Recognition errors, demonstrating that chain-of-thought reasoning hurts perception tasks
Clear presentation with thorough implementation details, comprehensive appendices, and strong reproducibility
Practical impact: SVE-Math-DeepSeek+ achieves 68.4% on MATHGLANCE vs 46.6% baseline; resources will benefit the research community
weaknesses: Limited generalization scope: 66% synthetic plane geometry; no evaluation on real-world mathematical diagrams from textbooks or scientific papers; solid geometry/graphs are reformatted from existing datasets rather than novel constructions
Missing critical human performance baseline despite claiming humans solve these 'at a glance'; even spot evaluation would strengthen claims significantly

Incomplete ablation: two-stage training (alignment + SFT) makes it unclear whether improvements come from better alignment or instruction SFT; Table 6 shows dramatic differences (MAVIS hurts reasoning by 27%) but lacks explanation
No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals despite having ~1,600 questions; single run per model without multiple seeds
Moderate downstream reasoning improvements (+4% on MathVista) insufficient to fully justify 200K training pairs; learning curves and minimum effective dataset size unknown
Text distractor vulnerability persists even in trained models (14% drop for SVE-Math-DeepSeek+), indicating fundamental over-reliance on language that GeoPeP only partially addresses
No cross-domain evaluation (e.g., train on plane geometry, test on graphs); generalization potential unclear
Missing inter-annotator agreement metrics for benchmark quality assessment; geometric clause verifier completeness not validated
